label: Al-Shabaab South-Central Corridor
notes: Principal Al-Shabaab movement corridor from Middle Jubba through Bay region to central Somalia; used for logistics, reinforcement, and tax collection

label: SNA Main Supply Route: Mogadishu–Baidoa
notes: Primary SNA logistics axis between capital and Southwest State; frequently targeted by Al-Shabaab IEDs and ambushes

label: SNA 2022 Offensive Axis: Mogadishu–Beledweyne
notes: Primary axis of advance for 2022 SNA/Macawisley Hiiraan offensive; route up Shabelle River valley

label: KDF Supply Corridor: Kenya Border–Kismayo
notes: Kenya Defence Forces logistics route from Kenyan border to Kismayo; critical for KDF ATMIS operations in Jubbaland

label: MV Ruen Mother-Ship Patrol Area (2023–24)
notes: Area of operations for pirate mother ship MV Ruen after hijacking Nov 2023; used for further attacks before Indian Navy retook vessel Mar 2024

label: Gulf of Aden International Shipping Lane
notes: Critical global shipping corridor; ~20,000 vessels/year; primary target of Somali piracy 2008-2012 and resurgence 2023-24

label: WFP Aid Corridor: Mogadishu–Bay Region
notes: World Food Programme and NGO aid supply route to drought-affected Bay and Bakool regions; negotiated access with armed actors required

label: Al-Shabaab Coastal Arms Smuggling Route
notes: Suspected arms smuggling route from Barawe coastal area toward Mogadishu hinterland; documented by UN Monitoring Group

label: SNA Axis: Kismayo–Baidoa
notes: SNA and KDF ATMIS operational axis connecting Jubbaland coast to Bay Region; key for coordinating southwest operations

label: IDP Displacement Flow: South Somalia–Mogadishu
notes: Primary displacement corridor; hundreds of thousands of IDPs fled conflict and drought in Lower Shabelle and Bay/Bakool toward Mogadishu settlements

label: ENDF Logistics: Ethiopia–Beledweyne Corridor
notes: Ethiopian military supply route from Ethiopia border through Hiiraan to Beledweyne; used by ENDF AMISOM/ATMIS contingent

label: Charcoal Export Route (UN Banned)
notes: Al-Shabaab charcoal export route via coastal dhows to Gulf states (UAE, Oman); banned under UNSC Resolution 2036 but documented violation by UN Monitoring Group

label: Maritime Supply: Mogadishu–Kismayo
notes: Maritime logistics route between Mogadishu and Kismayo; supplementary to overland routes and critical when roads are threatened by Al-Shabaab

label: EU NAVFOR Atalanta Patrol Zone
notes: EU NAVFOR counter-piracy patrol area covering Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean; WFP convoy escort missions also conducted within this zone

label: Al-Shabaab Kenya Border Infiltration
notes: Al-Shabaab cross-border movement corridor; used for attacks in Kenya's Northeast Province and to recruit Kenyan fighters (including for Westgate and Garissa attacks)

label: Operation Rolling Thunder / Hilaac — Lower Shabelle Axis
notes: Joint SNA and AUSSOM/UPDF Battle Group 44 ground offensive axis into Lower Shabelle launched Feb 28 – Mar 2, 2026. Operation Bader umbrella; sub-operation 'Hilaac' (Lightning) cleared Darasaalaam and Mubarak towns of al-Shabaab presence. Commanded by Brig. Gen. Jackson Kayanja. Bulunagaad joint operation (30+ killed) occurred along this corridor in late March 2026.

label: AFRICOM Airstrike: Al-Shabaab Near Xawaadleey (Mar 11, 2026)
notes: US Africa Command airstrike targeting al-Shabaab approximately 60 km north of Mogadishu near Xawaadleey. Conducted in coordination with the Federal Government of Somalia. Part of the intense 2026 airstrike campaign in Somalia (47+ strikes by mid-March). Origin shown from Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti.

label: AFRICOM Strikes: ISIS-Somalia, Golis Mountains (Mar 8/16/18, 2026)
notes: Multiple AFRICOM airstrikes targeting ISIS-Somalia in the Golis/Cal Miskaad Mountains, approximately 45–70 km southeast of Bossaso, Puntland. Strikes on March 8, 16, and 18, 2026 — authorized by Defense Secretary Hegseth at President Trump's direction. ISIS-Somalia operates from cave complexes in this mountain range. Origin shown from Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti.

label: AFRICOM Airstrike: Al-Shabaab NW of Kismayo (Mar 27, 2026)
notes: US Africa Command confirmed airstrike targeting Al-Shabaab approximately 132 km northwest of Kismayo (Jubbaland), conducted in coordination with the Federal Government of Somalia. Part of the intensified 2026 air campaign; US had conducted 43+ strikes in Somalia by early March 2026, pace tracking to exceed the 2025 record of 124 annual strikes. Origin shown from Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti. AFRICOM Press Release #36323.

label: SNA Offensive Axis: Mogadishu–Baidoa Seizure (Mar 30, 2026)
notes: SNA forces and allied 'South West Salvation' faction advanced along the Mogadishu–Baidoa corridor and seized Baidoa (Southwest State capital) on March 30, 2026, following the constitutional standoff with President Laftagareen. Ethiopian AUSSOM troops at Baidoa stood aside. SW State President Laftagareen resigned March 30. First federal military seizure of a state capital since independence. Significant civilian displacement (50,000+) reported by UNHCR.

label: SNA/Intl Airstrikes: Juba Regions Offensive (Apr 15–16, 2026)
notes: Coordinated airstrikes with 'international support' (consistent with AFRICOM-enabled operations) targeting Al-Shabaab in the Juba regions, Apr 15–16, 2026. Official toll: 54 Al-Shabaab fighters killed in airstrikes; additional 27 killed in ground operations by April 18. Target area: Middle Jubba/Jilib Al-Shabaab stronghold. Joint operation with Jubbaland forces. Origin shown from Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti.

label: SNA/Macawisley Counter-Offensive Axis: Beledweyne–Adan Yabal (Apr 21, 2026)
notes: Axis of planned SNA and Macawisley counter-offensive to retake Adan Yabal (seized by Al-Shabaab on April 19, 2026) from Beledweyne sector. President Mohamud ordered immediate operations on April 19; forces mobilizing from Beledweyne as of April 21. Approximately 100 Al-Shabaab fighters routed SNA from the town and surrounding outposts.

label: AFRICOM Strike: ISIS-Somalia SE of Bosaso (Apr 17, 2026) — Strike #56
notes: AFRICOM Press Release #36380 (announced April 19): Strike targeting ISIS-Somalia approximately 30 miles (48 km) SE of Bosaso, Puntland. The 56th US airstrike in Somalia in 2026 — an unprecedented pace (200+/year annualized). Targets ISIS-Somalia cave/mountain complexes in the Golis/Cal Miskaad range. Origin shown from Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti.

label: AFRICOM Airstrike #57: Al-Shabaab SW of Kismayo (Apr 21, 2026)
notes: AFRICOM Press Release #36382 (announced April 22): Strike targeting Al-Shabaab approximately 90 km southwest of Kismayo (Jubbaland), near Wadajir. The 57th US airstrike in Somalia in 2026 — on pace for 200+/year. Conducted in coordination with the Federal Government of Somalia. Origin shown from Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti.

label: Possible Piracy: Product Tanker SE of Xaafuun (Apr 22, 2026)
notes: EU NAVFOR Atalanta investigating possible armed boarding of a product tanker approximately 24 nautical miles southeast of Xaafuun (Hafun). Incident reported by Diaplous Group security consultants; investigation ongoing as of April 22. Part of resurgent piracy pattern active since October 2025. Atalanta patrols the Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean for WFP convoy escort and counter-piracy operations.

label: Al-Shabaab Mortar: Halane Camp (Apr 28, 2026)
notes: Al-Shabaab mortar attack targeting Halane base camp adjacent to Aden Adde Airport, Mogadishu, on April 28, 2026. AU/AUSSOM soldiers killed. Halane hosts AUSSOM HQ, UN offices, and Western missions. Origin from estimated Al-Shabaab firing position south of Mogadishu. Confirmed by Garowe Online and Somali Guardian.

label: AFRICOM Airstrike: Al-Shabaab NE of Kismayo (Apr 30, 2026)
notes: AFRICOM Press Release #36449: Strike targeting Al-Shabaab approximately 50km northeast of Kismayo (Jubbaland). Among 60+ US airstrikes in Somalia in 2026 — annualized pace of 200+/year. Conducted in coordination with the Federal Government of Somalia. Origin shown from Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti.

label: MT Eureka Hijacking Route: Yemen Shabwa → Somalia (May 2, 2026)
notes: Togo-flagged product tanker MT Eureka (3,300 DWT, Royal Shipping Lines/UAE) seized by ~9 Somali gunmen near Qana port off Yemen's Shabwa coast on May 2, 2026. Vessel carrying ~2,800 tons of diesel; crew of 12 (Egyptian and Indian nationals). Diverted across Gulf of Aden toward Somali coast. Third major hijacking in 10 days after Honour 25 (Apr 25) and Sward (Apr 27). JMIC elevated piracy threat to 'severe' May 1.

label: Honour 25 Hijack Route: Berbera → Puntland Coast (Apr 25, 2026)
notes: Route of Palau-flagged fuel tanker Honour 25 (3,000 DWT) from Berbera (Somaliland) toward Mogadishu, intercepted by at least 6 Somali pirates from Bandarbeyla district approximately 30 nautical miles offshore between Hafun (Xaafuun) and Bandarbeyla on April 25, 2026. Vessel carried 18,500 barrels of fuel; 17 multinational crew (10 Pakistanis, 4 Indonesians, 1 Indian, 1 Sri Lankan, 1 Myanmar national) taken hostage. Pirates anchored vessel off Puntland coast. EU NAVFOR Atalanta, Combined Task Force 151, and Spanish Joint Operations Command responding. Part of accelerating piracy resurgence since October 2025.

label: AFRICOM Strike #63: ISIS-Somalia SE of Bosaso (May 7, 2026)
notes: AFRICOM Press Release #36471 (announced May 7, 2026): Strike targeting ISIS-Somalia approximately 74km (46 miles) southeast of Bosaso near Miraale Well cave complex, Puntland. The 63rd US airstrike in Somalia in 2026, and the second strike in this exact area within 3 days (PR #36451 struck May 4). Part of the sustained campaign against ISIS-Somalia cave complexes in the Golis/Cal Miskaad mountain range. 2026 strike pace tracks to 200+/year. Origin shown from Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti.

label: AFRICOM Strike #62: ISIS-Somalia SE of Bosaso (May 4, 2026)
notes: AFRICOM Press Release #36451 (May 4, 2026): Strike targeting ISIS-Somalia approximately 46 miles (74 km) southeast of Bosaso, Puntland. The 62nd US airstrike in Somalia in 2026 — an unprecedented annual pace (200+/year annualized). Targeted ISIS-Somalia cave complexes in the Golis/Cal Miskaad mountain range. Conducted in coordination with the Federal Government of Somalia. Origin shown from Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti.

label: Al-Shabaab Seizure Axis: Moqokori (May 17, 2026)
notes: Al-Shabaab advance axis to briefly seize Moqokori town in Hiiraan Region on May 17, 2026. The seizure was described by WardheerNews as directly linked to Somalia's constitutional political crisis creating a security vacuum. Coordinated with insider killing of SNA 26th Brigade Commander Col. Hujale on the town's outskirts. Origin estimated from south Hiiraan rural Al-Shabaab hinterland.

label: Sward Hijacking Route: Gulf of Aden → Garacad (Apr 26, 2026)
notes: St Kitts-flagged cargo vessel Sward (carrying cement from Suez to Mombasa) intercepted by Somali pirates approximately 6 nautical miles northeast of Garacad on April 26, 2026. Crew of 15 (2 Indian nationals, 13 Syrians) taken hostage. Vessel diverted and anchored off Garacad — one of the original pirate-era anchorages from 2008-2012. Second of three simultaneous hijackings in 10 days (Honour 25 Apr 25, Sward Apr 26, MT Eureka May 2). As of May 21, 2026 (Day 25): vessel and crew still under pirate control; no ransom paid.

label: Three-Vessel Piracy Crisis: Eyl–Garacad Anchor Zone (May 2026)
notes: As of May 22, 2026 (Day 27/26/20): Honour 25 anchored off Eyl area, Puntland (17 crew, Day 27, $3M ransom demand unanswered); Sward anchored off Garacad (15 crew, Day 26); MT Eureka held in Puntland coastal waters (12 crew, Day 20, $10M demand unanswered). Total: 44 hostages, no ransom paid, no rescue attempted. ISS Africa (May 18, 2026) warned of 'unprecedented strategic risk' as Iran War depletes EU NAVFOR Atalanta and CTF-151 counter-piracy capacity. JMIC 'severe' threat level. Worst simultaneous piracy crisis since 2012.

label: Al-Shabaab Hiiraan Pressure: Consolidation in Adan Yabal (May 2026)
notes: Al-Shabaab consolidation axis in Hiiraan Region: Adan Yabal (seized April 19, Day 32 as of May 21) and Moqokori pressure corridor. No SNA counter-offensive materialized despite President Mohamud's April 19 order. Political crisis in Mogadishu has paralyzed military command. Al-Shabaab reinforcing IED belts and defensive positions at Adan Yabal. ACLED data shows highest Hiiraan conflict event pace since September 2022.

label: Three-Vessel Piracy Crisis: Day 32/31/25 — 44 Hostages (May 27, 2026)
notes: As of May 27, 2026 (Day 32/31/25): Honour 25 anchored off Eyl/Puntland coast (17 crew, Day 32, $3M demand; crew conditions critical — one daily rice meal, no water, no medicine); Sward anchored off Garacad (15 crew, Day 31); MT Eureka held off Bandarbeyla, Puntland (12 crew including 8 Egyptians, Day 25, $10M demand). Total: 44 hostages, no ransom paid, no rescue attempted. Egypt's formal May 25 demand on Somalia's FGS remained unmet. EU NAVFOR and CTF-151 continue to be diverted by Iran War. FDD confirmed Iran-backed Houthi weapons/GPS supply to pirates. JMIC 'severe' threat level. Worst simultaneous piracy crisis since 2012.

label: Al-Shabaab Adan Yabal Hold — Day 38 (May 27, 2026)
notes: Al-Shabaab continues to hold Adan Yabal (Aadan Yabaal), Hiiraan Region, for Day 38 as of May 27, 2026 — extending the longest uncontested insurgent occupation of a Hiiraan town since the 2022 SNA/Macawisley offensive. No SNA counter-offensive materialized despite President Mohamud's April 19 emergency order. ICG Briefing B208 (May 25) and ISS Africa (May 20) explicitly link Somalia's political paralysis (opposition countdown Day 12) to Al-Shabaab's ability to consolidate this territorial gain. Al-Shabaab has reinforced IED belts and defensive positions, making any retake operation increasingly costly.

label: Piracy: Bandarbeyla–Garacad Hostage Anchorage Zone Day 33/32/26 (May 28)
notes: As of May 28, 2026 (Day 33/32/26): Honour 25 (17 crew, $3M demand, crew conditions critical) and MT Eureka (12 crew including 8 Egyptians, $10M demand) both anchored near Bandarbeyla; Sward (15 crew, Syrian and Indian nationals) held off Garacad. Total: 44 hostages, no ransom paid, no rescue operation launched. Egypt's May 25 FGS demand unmet. EU NAVFOR/CTF-151 diverted by Iran War; Houthi weapons/GPS supply to pirates confirmed (FDD). JMIC 'severe' threat level. Worst simultaneous piracy crisis since 2012.

label: Al-Shabaab Adan Yabal Hold — Day 39 (May 28, 2026)
notes: Al-Shabaab continues to hold Adan Yabal (Aadan Yabaal), Hiiraan Region, for Day 39 as of May 28, 2026 — extending the longest uncontested insurgent occupation of a Hiiraan town since the 2022 SNA/Macawisley offensive. Somalia's new Galmudug election crisis (NISA Director Mahad Salad candidacy) and opposition countdown Day 13 continue to paralyze military command-and-control. No SNA counter-offensive launched despite 39 days since President Mohamud's April 19 emergency retake order. Al-Shabaab IED belts and reinforced defensive positions at Adan Yabal make future SNA assault increasingly costly.

label: Three-Vessel Piracy Crisis: Day 36/35/29 — 44 Hostages (May 31, 2026)
notes: As of May 31, 2026 (Day 36/35/29): Honour 25 anchored near Bandarbeyla, Puntland (17 crew, Day 36, $3M demand; crew in critical condition — minimal food, no clean water, no medicine); Sward anchored off Garacad (15 crew, Day 35); MT Eureka held off Puntland coast (12 crew including 8 Egyptians, Day 29, $10M demand). Total: 44 hostages, no ransom paid, no rescue attempted. Jubbaland's formal withdrawal from Somalia's federal system (May 31) deepens political paralysis preventing FGS response. EU NAVFOR/CTF-151 diverted by Iran War; Houthi weapons/GPS supply to pirates confirmed by FDD and UN Panel. JMIC 'severe' threat level. Worst simultaneous piracy crisis since 2012.

label: Al-Shabaab Adan Yabal Hold — Day 42 (May 31, 2026)
notes: Al-Shabaab continues to hold Adan Yabal (Aadan Yabaal), Hiiraan Region, for Day 42 as of May 31, 2026 — the longest uncontested insurgent occupation of a Hiiraan town since the 2022 SNA/Macawisley offensive. Jubbaland's withdrawal from the federal system and the opposition countdown Day 16 deepen the political paralysis paralyzing military command-and-control from Mogadishu. No SNA counter-offensive has been launched despite 42 days since President Mohamud's April 19 emergency retake order. Al-Shabaab IED belts and reinforced defensive positions make any future SNA assault increasingly costly.

label: Three-Vessel Piracy Crisis: Day 37/36/30 — 44 Hostages (Jun 1, 2026)
notes: As of June 1, 2026 (Day 37/36/30): Honour 25 anchored near Bandarbeyla, Puntland (17 crew, Day 37, $3M demand; crew in critical condition — minimal food, no clean water, no medicine); Sward anchored off Garacad (15 crew, Day 36); MT Eureka held off Puntland coast (12 crew including 8 Egyptians, Day 30, $10M demand). Total: 44 hostages, no ransom paid, no rescue attempted. Egypt's May 25 FGS demand unmet. SNA Gedo deployment (700+ Turkish-trained troops) adds military dimension to post-Jubbaland-withdrawal crisis. EU NAVFOR/CTF-151 diverted by Iran War; Houthi weapons/GPS supply to pirates confirmed. JMIC 'severe' threat level. Worst simultaneous piracy crisis since 2012.

label: Al-Shabaab Adan Yabal Hold — Day 43 (Jun 1, 2026)
notes: Al-Shabaab continues to hold Adan Yabal (Aadan Yabaal), Hiiraan Region, for Day 43 as of June 1, 2026 — extending the longest uncontested insurgent occupation of a Hiiraan town since the 2022 SNA/Macawisley offensive. SNA Gedo deployment controversy and Jubbaland's post-federal-withdrawal stance now create a secondary military-political crisis that further divides SNA command attention. Opposition countdown Day 17 (13 days before threatened parallel authority) and approaching Galmudug elections (June 20) deepen the political paralysis. Al-Shabaab IED belts and reinforced defensive positions at Adan Yabal make any future SNA assault increasingly costly. ICG Briefing B208 warns political paralysis is directly enabling territorial consolidation.

label: SNA Gedo Region Deployment (Turkish-Trained Troops, Jun 1, 2026)
notes: Axis of SNA deployment of 700+ Turkish-trained soldiers into Gedo Region (Bardhere, Balad-Hawo, Dolow districts), Jubbaland, by June 2026. Jubbaland State — having formally withdrawn from Somalia's federal compact on May 31 — treats the deployment as a foreign military incursion into its territory, triggering protests and diplomatic confrontation. Kenya's KDF (AUSSOM Sector 2 commander) is the longstanding external security guarantee for Jubbaland. The SNA deployment adds a military escalation dimension to the political standoff.

label: Mogadishu Urban Warfare: Government Forces vs. Opposition (Jun 4, 2026)
notes: Axis of government heavy weapons deployment during June 4, 2026 urban warfare in Mogadishu — the worst security crisis in the capital in more than a decade. Government forces deployed heavy artillery against opposition-aligned positions near Dabka Junction and surrounding residential districts. UN Secretary-General Guterres expressed alarm; US called for restraint. Violence began June 3 with a gunfight between government forces and security guards of former PM Hassan Ali Khaire. On June 5, the government claimed to have restored order in two districts; Turkish F-16s flew over the capital during mass protests.

label: 4th Piracy Hijacking: Gulf of Aden → Garacad (Jun 5, 2026)
notes: A fourth cargo vessel was reportedly hijacked off the coast of Garacad on June 5, 2026, per Al Jazeera reporting on Somalia's deepening political and maritime crisis. Vessel, flag state, crew nationality, and ransom demand not confirmed at time of report. Diverted toward Garacad anchorage — one of the primary pirate-era anchorages from 2008-2012 and current anchorage of the Sward (Day 40). Brings total simultaneous vessels in pirate hands to potentially 4, with 44+ crew members captive — approaching the worst simultaneous piracy crisis since 2012. EU NAVFOR Atalanta and CTF-151 remain diverted by Iran War; Houthi weapons/GPS supply to pirates confirmed.

label: Al-Shabaab Assault on Ceel Dheere, Galmudug (Jun 8, 2026)
notes: Al-Shabaab fighters attacked government positions in Ceel Dheere town, Galmudug State, briefly overrunning SNA army positions before troops pushed them back toward Ali Yabal village. Government claimed 47 militants killed vs. 5 soldiers lost (unverified). ICG CrisisWatch called it the most significant Galmudug attack since March 2026.

label: AFRICOM Strike: Al-Shabaab near Kurtunwaarey (Jun 14, 2026) — Ends 40-Day Pause
notes: First US airstrike in Somalia since May 6, 2026, ending a ~40-day pause. Part of a cluster of at least 4 AFRICOM strikes across Lower Shabelle/Lower Juba over the following week (Kurtunwaarey, Route 109 NW of Kismayo, near Welmaro).

label: Danab Special Forces Raid: Kuntuwaarey District (Jun 15, 2026) — 14 Killed
notes: Danab special forces killed 14 Al-Shabaab fighters in a targeted raid in Kuntuwaarey district, Lower Shabelle, destroying a weapons/explosives cache. No SNA casualties disclosed.

label: AFRICOM Strike: Al-Shabaab near Qumbi (Jul 13, 2026) — 88km NW of Kismayo
notes: Part of a cluster with the Sablaale strike the same night; reported as roughly the 74th US airstrike in Somalia in 2026, on pace to exceed 2025's record of ~124-126 strikes.

label: AFRICOM Strike: Al-Shabaab near Sablaale (Jul 13, 2026) — 190km SW of Mogadishu
notes: Same night, Danab Commandos conducted a ground raid in Sablaale district killing 7 Al-Shabaab fighters including a senior commander, destroying two training/propaganda facilities.

label: Danab Ground Raid: Sablaale District (Jul 13, 2026) — 7 Killed Incl. Senior Commander
notes: Ground raid destroyed two Al-Shabaab training/propaganda facilities in Sablaale district, Lower Shabelle, same night as the AFRICOM strikes near Qumbi and Sablaale.

label: SNA/International Partner Strikes: Middle Shabelle (Jul 13, 2026) — 26 Killed
notes: Somali security forces, 'in collaboration with international partners,' struck Al-Shabaab positions in the Adow Jilib, Gayfo and Qordheere areas of Middle Shabelle, killing 26 militants and destroying one armored vehicle and one fuel tanker.

label: SNA 61st Battalion Sweep: Eight Villages, Sablaale District (Jul 15, 2026)
notes: Clearing operation across eight villages in Sablaale district (Faytaan, Sadex, Aqab, Wabi Goof, Buula Doon, Baroodooy, Xaliima, Yaalo), destroying Al-Shabaab hideouts. No casualties/arrests reported; claims not independently verified.

label: MV Golden Arsenal Piracy Attempt Repelled, Gulf of Aden (Jul 1, 2026)
notes: Bulk carrier Golden Arsenal (21 crew) boarded by 4 armed pirates ~300nm ENE of Djibouti; crew locked in citadel, pirates damaged bridge but could not breach it. INS Trikand and MARCOS commandos, backed by a P-8I patrol aircraft, repelled the pirates; vessel resumed voyage with no injuries. First hijacking attempt since MT Eureka's seizure in early May.

label: Federal Forces Defend Baidoa Against VBIED Assault (Aug 17, 2026)
notes: Federal government forces repelled a pre-dawn VBIED assault on Baidoa by militia loyal to former Southwest State president Laftagareen (reportedly coordinating with Al-Shabaab), killing 30+ attackers on Aug 17, 2026; fighting continued into Aug 18 as opposition fighters were driven from the city.

label: Sibu 1 / Seamull Redirected Toward Puntland Coast (Aug 20, 2026)
notes: The sanctioned tanker Sibu 1 (ex-Seamull), hijacked ~136nm east of Al Mukalla, Yemen, was steered toward Somalia's Puntland coast after six pirates boarded on Aug 20, 2026. Sixth vessel held in the 2026 piracy resurgence; all 20 crew (16 Indian) reported safe.
